questions.text: Thanks for doing the dishes.
questions.imageAlt: A stick figure at a kitchen counter with plates and rising steam.

questions.text: Let’s focus on refining your presentation skills step by step.
questions.imageAlt: A stick figure pointing at a slide deck on a screen.

questions.text: You need to listen better in meetings.
questions.imageAlt: Two stick figures in a meeting, one gesturing toward a whiteboard.

questions.text: Don't let this setback discourage you—you’re doing great!
questions.imageAlt: A stick figure waving beside a small hill and a sun.

questions.text: Your progress on the project exceeded the expected timeline.
questions.imageAlt: A line chart climbing across a project board.

questions.text: That report was outstanding, fantastic job!
questions.imageAlt: A stick figure holding up a report with a star nearby.

questions.text: You really struggle to handle conflict effectively.
questions.imageAlt: Two stick figures facing each other, one with a thought bubble.

questions.text: When you interrupt our meetings, it creates confusion and slows progress.
questions.imageAlt: Three stick figures at a meeting table, one mid-gesture.

questions.text: You asked two questions and answered them yourself before anyone else had a chance to answer.
questions.evilNote: This is an observation that could be used as a starting point for feedback, but on its own it doesn't provide any guidance or judgment. It could be perceived as passive-aggressive or as a veiled criticism without offering any constructive advice.
questions.imageAlt: A stick figure with two speech bubbles, both coming from the same person.

questions.text: If I were you, I’d start preparing the slides at least a week in advance to avoid the last-minute rush.
questions.imageAlt: A stick figure pointing at slides and a calendar.

questions.text: You might want to consider using a password manager to keep your credentials secure.
questions.imageAlt: A stick figure pointing at a phone with a lock on the screen.

questions.text: I suggest you BCC the manager on these types of emails just to keep them in the loop.
questions.imageAlt: An email window with an extra address being added.

questions.text: Have you thought about blocking out your calendar for deep work? It really helped me focus.
questions.imageAlt: A stick figure pointing at a calendar with one block filled in.

questions.text: Thank you for jumping in to help with the client call today; your expertise really saved the deal.
questions.imageAlt: Two stick figures on a call beside a client document.

questions.text: I really appreciate you taking the time to explain the codebase to the new interns.
questions.imageAlt: A stick figure pointing at code while another watches.

questions.text: Thanks for keeping the kitchen clean this week; it makes a huge difference for everyone.
questions.imageAlt: A tidy kitchen counter and a stick figure with a cloth.

questions.text: I’m grateful for your patience while I was navigating that difficult personal situation.
questions.imageAlt: Two stick figures, one holding a small note, a thought bubble overhead.

questions.text: Next time, let's look at how you can structure the opening of your pitch to grab attention faster.
questions.imageAlt: A stick figure pointing at the top line of a pitch slide.

questions.text: I’d like to work with you on refining your delegation skills so you can focus more on strategy.
questions.imageAlt: A stick figure beside three task boxes on a board.

questions.text: Think about how you could have handled that objection differently to keep the conversation open.
questions.imageAlt: Two stick figures talking, with a curved arrow between them.

questions.text: Let’s pair up on the next module so I can show you some shortcuts in the new framework.
questions.imageAlt: Two stick figures sharing a keyboard in front of a code window.

questions.text: Your report was disorganized and contained several factual errors that we had to fix.
questions.imageAlt: A document with a red X in the corner.

questions.text: Your lack of contribution during the brainstorming session was quite noticeable.
questions.imageAlt: Four stick figures at a whiteboard, one standing still.

questions.text: You’ve got this! The progress you've made over the last month has been incredible.
questions.imageAlt: A stick figure looking up a rising line.

questions.text: Don't let this setback discourage you; I've seen what you're capable of when you're at your best.
questions.imageAlt: A stick figure beside a dip in a line and a small chart.

questions.text: Keep going—you are so close to cracking the solution to this bug.
questions.imageAlt: A stick figure at a terminal with a squiggle still on the screen.

questions.text: I believe in your ability to lead this project, even if it feels a bit overwhelming right now.
questions.imageAlt: A stick figure pointing at a project board.

questions.text: Based on our metrics, you met all your KPIs for the quarter with a 10% margin.
questions.imageAlt: A metrics sheet with rows of numbers and a small circle.

questions.text: Your performance on the last project was slightly below the expected standard for your seniority.
questions.imageAlt: A chart with a dashed target line and a wandering actual line.

questions.text: You’ve consistently delivered high-quality work that aligns perfectly with our brand guidelines.
questions.imageAlt: A document with a check mark at the bottom.

questions.text: In comparison to the rest of the team, your output volume is currently in the top tier.
questions.imageAlt: A bar chart with one tall bar.

questions.text: Fantastic job on that presentation! You really knocked it out of the park.
questions.imageAlt: A stick figure in front of a presentation screen and a star.

questions.text: You are such a natural leader; the way you handled that conflict was brilliant.
questions.imageAlt: Three stick figures under a line, one pointing.

questions.text: That was an incredibly elegant solution to a very messy problem.
questions.imageAlt: A tangled line straightening into a neat box.

questions.text: You have a real gift for making complex topics sound simple.
questions.imageAlt: A dense page of marks turning into a short simple box.

questions.text: When you interrupt me in front of clients, I feel undermined and it makes me lose my confidence.
questions.imageAlt: Three stick figures at a client table, one gesturing.

questions.text: I felt really supported when you spoke up for my idea after everyone else dismissed it.
questions.imageAlt: A stick figure raising a hand beside a small idea card.

questions.text: It makes me feel anxious when you change the project deadlines without discussing it with me first.
questions.imageAlt: A calendar with a dashed date and a stick figure looking on.

questions.text: I really enjoy collaborating with you because your energy makes the work feel less like a chore.
questions.imageAlt: Two stick figures waving beside a shared task card.

questions.text: I think you should come into the office earlier.
questions.imageAlt: An office door, a stick figure, and a clock.

questions.text: You never seem to be ready when the meeting starts, and it’s disrespectful to everyone's time.
questions.evilNote: This uses shaming language ('disrespectful') rather than focusing on the impact of the behavior.
questions.imageAlt: Stick figures at a meeting table under a clock.

questions.text: Your deep-seated fear of rejection is preventing you from taking the risks necessary for growth.
questions.evilNote: Armchair psychology. Assigning deep-seated psychological motives to a peer is often a form of boundary-crossing or bullying.
questions.imageAlt: A stick figure, a thought bubble, and a rising line.

questions.text: You seem to have an avoidant personality when it comes to dealing with direct conflict.
questions.evilNote: Labeling a colleague with a 'personality type' to explain away their behavior is reductive and unprofessional.
questions.imageAlt: Two stick figures, one a step back from the other.

questions.text: I think your subconscious bias against the marketing team is clouding your judgment.
questions.evilNote: This is a 'masked' criticism that attacks the person's character and subconscious rather than their specific actions.
questions.imageAlt: A stick figure pointing at a board labeled with rows of marks.

questions.text: Your need for constant external validation is starting to affect the team's velocity.
questions.evilNote: Pathologizing a teammate's work style ('need for validation') is a high-conflict feedback tactic.
questions.imageAlt: Three stick figures and a small circle overhead.

questions.text: The tone of your last email was overly aggressive and unprofessional.
questions.evilNote: Using subjective, loaded labels like 'aggressive' without providing specific examples can feel like an attack rather than constructive help.
questions.imageAlt: An email window with one heavy line of text.

questions.text: Your need to fit in is preventing you from generating good results.
questions.evilNote: This focuses on a perceived character flaw rather than objective performance metrics.
questions.imageAlt: A row of stick figures under a shared bar.

questions.text: The deploy pipeline failed twice this morning. The last green build was yesterday at 16:40.
questions.imageAlt: A stick-figure engineer staring at a build monitor with a red X and a clock.

questions.text: If I were you, I'd put the flaky integration test behind a retry before the next release train.
questions.imageAlt: A stick figure pointing at a train made of brackets while a flask wobbles.

questions.text: Thanks for staying on the incident bridge until the pager went quiet. I know that ate your evening.
questions.imageAlt: Two stick figures on a late call, one holding a quiet pager.

questions.text: Let's pair on the next PR and walk the diff together so the review comments get smaller over time.
questions.imageAlt: Two stick figures sharing one keyboard in front of a diff.

questions.text: You keep merging without waiting for the required reviewer, and it is making the rest of us look careless.
questions.evilNote: This piles a character judgment ('careless') onto the team instead of naming the specific process miss and its effect.
questions.imageAlt: A stick figure stamping a pull request while another waits.

questions.text: That outage was rough, but you've shipped three clean rollbacks since. Don't let one red dashboard talk you out of the next change.
questions.imageAlt: A stick figure looking at a dashboard that is mostly green with one red square.

questions.text: Against the sprint goal, four of the five acceptance criteria are met. The fifth is still blocked on the API contract.
questions.imageAlt: A checklist with several ticks and one box still open beside a plug.

questions.text: The way you wrote that incident timeline is the clearest write-up this team has produced all quarter.
questions.imageAlt: A stick figure holding a timeline with a small star nearby.

questions.text: You are clearly conflict-avoidant, which is why you never push back in architecture reviews.
questions.evilNote: Diagnosing a personality trait ('conflict-avoidant') substitutes armchair psychology for a specific, observable behavior.
questions.imageAlt: Stick figures at an architecture board, one with a question-mark bubble.

questions.text: When you answer in the thread before I've finished the question, I lose the thread and the rest of the channel goes quiet.
questions.imageAlt: A chat window where one reply lands before the other line is finished.
